title: Support Worker - Mental Health
company: P+S Care and Support Services - Agency - Permanent
description:
Location: West Essex Harlow and Waltham Abbey
Salary: £26,298.11 per annum
Hours: 37.5 hours per week
Contract: Permanent, full-time

About the Role

P&S Care & Support is recruiting a Flexible Support Worker on behalf of a client providing mental health support services across West Essex.

This is an opportunity to make a real difference in people's lives by supporting adults with enduring mental health needs as they work towards recovery, greater independence and improved wellbeing.

You will support individuals transitioning from hospital back into their homes and communities, helping them rebuild confidence, develop practical life skills and achieve their personal goals.

The service focuses on recovery-oriented support, encouraging individuals to become more independent and resilient while reducing their reliance on hospital admissions and other medical interventions where possible.

You will work with individuals over a recovery period of up to 24 months, providing tailored support to help them make positive and sustainable changes to their lives.

Key Responsibilities

You will provide practical, social and emotional support to individuals in their homes and within the community, helping them develop the skills and confidence needed to live more independently.

Responsibilities will include supporting individuals to maintain their tenancies, manage housing-related issues, access welfare benefits and engage with relevant community services.

You will work collaboratively with mental health professionals, housing providers and other external agencies to ensure individuals receive appropriate support.

You will also help individuals identify and work towards their recovery goals, monitor progress against support plans, contribute to risk assessments and maintain accurate records.

The role may involve supporting people with complex needs, including dual diagnosis, and helping them access appropriate mental health and substance misuse services.

You will encourage individuals to develop practical and social skills, access education or employment opportunities where appropriate, and become more involved in their communities.

Successful candidates will be required to work across two services in West Essex, covering Harlow and Waltham Abbey. Flexibility to travel between service locations is therefore essential.

Working Pattern

This is a permanent, full-time position working 37.5 hours per week on a seven-day rolling rota.

The role operates on a three-week rolling shift pattern, consisting of early shifts from 8:00am to 4:00pm and late shifts from 1:30pm to 9:30pm.

You will be required to work two weekends every three weeks.

Although these are the standard shift patterns, some flexibility may be required to meet the needs of the service.

About You

We are looking for a compassionate, motivated and resilient individual who is passionate about supporting people with mental health needs to achieve greater independence.

You should have experience working with adults with enduring mental health needs or within a similar support environment, together with an understanding of recovery-focused support.

You will need strong communication and interpersonal skills, the ability to build positive professional relationships and a sensitive, non-judgemental approach.

An understanding of housing management, complex needs and dual diagnosis would be beneficial.

You should be confident working independently, managing your workload and maintaining professional boundaries. The ability to recognise when someone may be experiencing difficulties and require additional support is also important.

A flexible approach to working hours and locations is essential, alongside a commitment to ongoing learning and professional development.

Benefits

The position offers a range of benefits, including:
- Access to an employee benefits platform offering discounts, wellbeing support and online GP services.
- Death-in-service benefit of twice your annual salary.
- Workplace pension scheme, with automatic enrolment after three months.
- 22 days' annual leave plus statutory bank holidays, increasing to 25 days after three years of continuous service.
- Company sick pay after 12 months of continuous service.
- Mandatory training and opportunities for professional development.

Please note: The employer is unable to offer visa sponsorship. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK without sponsorship.

An enhanced DBS check, right-to-work checks and employment checks will be required.

How to Apply

If you have relevant experience and are passionate about supporting people with mental health needs to achieve greater independence, we would love to hear from you.

Please submit your applicant through CV Library and one of the P&S Care and Support team will get back to you!

Male Residential Support Workers x 3, Children's Learning Disability Home, Waltham Abbey, Essex

13.50 per hour plus 60 per sleep-in Full-time, permanent Rota including days, evenings, weekends and sleep-ins

We're recruiting three experienced, resilient male Residential Support Workers for a well-established, Ofsted-registered children's home in Waltham Abbey supporting young people with learning disabilities and autism. You'll be a positive, consistent role model for young people who need adults they can trust, with structure, patience and the confidence to stay calm when things get tough.

What you'll do
- Provide day-to-day care, guidance and emotional support, helping young people build routine, confidence, communication and independence skills
- Act as a positive male role model, using de-escalation, positive behaviour support and relationship-based approaches to support behaviour that challenges

- Keep accurate daily logs and incident reports to Ofsted standards

- At least 12 months' experience in an Ofsted-registered children's residential home, ideally supporting young people with learning disabilities and/or autism (supported accommodation, adult care or school settings alone won't count)
- Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare, or willingness to complete it
- Physical and emotional resilience, with experience of de-escalation and positive behaviour support (PMVA, MAPA or Team Teach an advantage)
- The right to work in the UK. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship.
- Willingness to work a flexible rota including sleep-ins
- A full UK driving licence is highly desirable

What's on offer
- 13.50 per hour plus 60 per sleep-in
- Ongoing training and support with qualifications
- A supportive management team and a real chance to make a difference
- Enhanced DBS provided

This role is open to male applicants only. Being male is an occupational requirement for this post under Schedule 9, Part 1 of the Equality Act 2010, to meet the needs of the young people currently living in the home.

title: Support Worker
description:
Are you an experienced Residential Support Worker looking for flexible agency work?

We are currently recruiting experienced and reliable Residential Support Workers to support vulnerable children and young people across a range of residential care settings.

The young people you will support may have experienced trauma or difficult life circumstances and may present with challenging behaviours, autism, emotional and behavioural difficulties and complex support needs.

This is a rewarding opportunity for caring and resilient individuals who want to make a positive difference while enjoying the flexibility of agency work.

The Role

As a Residential Support Worker, you will provide high-quality care and support to children and young people, helping them feel safe, supported and valued.

Your responsibilities may include:
- Providing day-to-day care and support to vulnerable children and young people
- Building positive and trusting relationships
- Supporting young people with their daily routines and individual needs
- Engaging children in activities, hobbies and interests
- Supporting emotional wellbeing and personal development
- Managing and responding appropriately to challenging behaviours
- Supporting children with autism and other additional needs
- Following individual care plans and risk assessments
- Maintaining professional boundaries and providing consistent support

Every shift will be different, and you may work with young people with a range of needs and backgrounds. You will need to be adaptable, patient and able to remain calm and professional in challenging situations.

Flexible Agency Shifts

Agency work gives you the flexibility to work around your existing commitments, with shifts available across a range of residential childcare settings.

You must be able to work flexible hours, which may include long day shifts, weekends, bank holidays and sleep ins. Flexibility is essential, as shift patterns and requirements will vary depending on the home and the needs of the young people.

About You

We are looking for people who are:
- Calm and emotionally resilient
- Confident supporting children with challenging behaviours
- Comfortable working with children and young people with autism and additional needs
- Reliable and professional
- Able to adapt to different care environments
- Passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of vulnerable young people

Requirements

To be considered for these agency opportunities, you will need:
- To be 21 years of age or over
- At least 6 months' experience working with children or young people in a residential setting
- A clean UK driving licence
- The flexibility to work long days, weekends and sleep-in shifts when required
- A genuine commitment to working with vulnerable children and young people

Why Work With Us?
- Flexible temporary agency shifts
- Opportunity to work across a variety of residential childcare settings
- Gain experience working with children with a range of complex needs
- Build your experience within the residential childcare sector
- Potential opportunities for ongoing and permanent work
- Support from your dedicated recruitment team
- Opportunity to make a genuine difference to vulnerable young people's lives

If you're an experienced Residential Support Worker looking for flexible agency work and are passionate about supporting children and young people, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to discuss available shifts and opportunities in your area.

As a Care Support Worker at Peabody, you'll be a vital part of someone's journey, helping them live independently, confidently, and joyfully. Whether it's supporting with daily routines, encouraging hobbies, or simply being a kind presence, you'll help people feel safe, heard, and empowered.

No previous care experience is required. If you have the right values, a positive attitude, and a genuine desire to support others, we'll provide the training and support you need to succeed.

Please state clearly on your application whether you are applying for the full-time (37.5 hours) or part-time (15 hours) position.

What You'll Do
- Support people with personal care, health needs, and daily living tasks
- Encourage independence, choice, hobbies, and community involvement
- Build positive relationships with customers, families, and professionals
- Help maintain safe, comfortable homes while keeping accurate records

What You'll Need
- A kind, compassionate approach and a positive outlook
- Good communication skills and the ability to work as part of a team
- Flexibility to work a 24/7 rota, including evenings, weekends, bank holidays, and overnight shifts

A full, clean UK manual driving licence is essential

Please Read Before Applying

This role operates on a 24/7 working pattern, including overnight shifts, weekends, and bank holidays. You'll need to be flexible and ready to support people when they need you most.

Experience isn't essential, but a full, clean UK manual driving licence is. If you're caring, reliable, and ready to make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you.

Please apply now by submitting an anonymised CV and a short statement explaining why you're the perfect fit for this role.

Interviews will be held on 19th & 20th November 2026

title: Night Enabling Support Worker
description:
Night Enabling Support Worker

Location: Southend on Sea

Salary: £13.15 per hour

Vacancy Type: Permanent, Part Time (30 hours per week)

Are you the candidate we are looking for? At Shaftesbury Kenway Court we are recruiting for 2 part time Night Enabling Support Workers.

Please note this role does not qualify for visa sponsorship, as the salary requirements set by the Home Office are not satisfied.

We are looking for people with the passion, talent, skills and experience that all add up to a caring and community-minded workforce.

We believe that the people we support have the right to a full and flourishing life. They deserve the very best in delivery. Driven by our core values, Shaftesbury strives to be Open, Enabling, Inclusive and Courageous in all that we do.

Our disability services across adult care, children s care and education are all focused on inclusion and support. Committed to professional, flexible and personalised care, we are passionate about going the extra mile in providing opportunities for people to thrive and live well.

About the role

As a Night Enabling Support Worker it will be your role to provide support and encouragement, by taking direction from both the person supported and the person centred support plan.

You will be required to maintain accurate records while at work in line with the service requirements. You may also be required to administer personal care and medication.

Kenway Court is a residential, community-focused care home in Southend-on-Sea.

The service supports people with intellectual and physical disabilities. People who live at Kenway Court have wide individual choice, with active support from staff. Our service offers nursing support to those with complex needs.

We take a person-centred, flexible approach. We know that everyone s needs and aspirations are different that all sorts of things add up to a flourishing life.

Benefits of working at Shaftesbury

At Shaftesbury, we know that our workers are our greatest asset. We re proud to have some of the best and most committed staff in the sector and we want to attract more people like you to work with Shaftesbury. We re now offering even more great benefits to reward the work of our wonderful staff in adult care:
- Welcome to Shaftesbury bonus of £500 on completion of 12 months of employment (terms apply)
- Happy Birthday to you! As well as sending you a birthday card, all frontline care staff can have the opportunity to take the day off on their birthday, taken from your annual entitlement.
- Great CQC, great reward. If your service is rated good or equivalent by CQC in all domains, all staff will receive a £30 gift voucher. If rated outstanding, all staff will receive a £50 gift voucher.
- We want to reward staff in a range of ways for their hard work. You can be nominated for a recognition letter from a member of the Executive Leadership Team and you may also be nominated to receive a gift voucher up to £50 for going above and beyond within your role.
- Excellent training package provided for all staff.
- Generous Annual Leave entitlement of 25 days + 8 days bank holiday for the first 5 years. Increasing to 28 days + 8 days bank holiday after 5 years.
- Pension Scheme.
- Access to our employee assistance program.

Shaftesbury is the disability charity that s committed to enabling children, young people and adults to live a life that adds up for them.

What makes life liveable is never down to just one thing - it s the sum of many things. From friendship to fun; from companionship to community; from a great chat to a challenge overcome, it all adds up to Shaftesbury.

Through a wide range of disability care, special education, and rehabilitation services we promote inclusion and wellbeing for all. Together, we work to see people take part, contribute and be valued. We put the elements in place that all add up to connected lives.

Shaftesbury is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable children and adults and expects all employees to share this commitment. All offers of employment are subject to an enhanced DBS/Access NI check.

Shaftesbury is committed to the Disability Confident Scheme and to equal opportunities therefore we welcome and encourage applications from everyone regardless of age, disability, gender, ethnicity, religion and sexual orientation.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Shaftesbury Group, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

title: Therapeutic Residential Children's Home Waking Night Support Worker
description:
Salary range - £29,000 to £33,600 / £13.33 to £15.38

Night shift workers: 42 hours per week

At Bear Care, we believe every child deserves to feel safe, understood and supported to build a positive future.

We care for children who may have experienced trauma, disrupted relationships and significant challenges in their lives. Our aim is to provide a safe, stable and nurturing environment where children can build trust, develop emotional resilience and make progress at their own pace.

We are looking for warm, approachable and emotionally mature people who genuinely want to make a difference. Previous residential childcare experience is valuable, but it is not essential for the right candidate.

What we offer

We want our employees to feel supported, valued and able to develop throughout their career. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:
- Annual leave that increases with length of service
- Complimentary Perkbox membership, giving access to a range of discounts, rewards and wellbeing benefits
- Complimentary access to counselling services
- Long service awards
- Free parking
- Refer a friend bonus
- Funded CPD and ongoing learning opportunities
- Career development and progression opportunities
- A supportive working environment

About the role

As a Residential Support Worker, you will:
- Provide emotional and social support, helping children and young people build positive and meaningful relationships.
- Support day-to-day routines including waking, mealtimes, school or college, activities and bedtime.
- Encourage participation in hobbies, activities and the local community.
- Build trusted and consistent relationships as a key worker for allocated children.
- Put our Therapeutic Framework into practice through your everyday interactions and support.
- Support children and young people to develop age-appropriate independence and life skills.
- Prepare meals and contribute to cooking, cleaning, shopping and laundry within the home.
- Promote the safety, welfare and wellbeing of children and young people at all times.
- Contribute to care plans, risk assessments and reviews, and maintain accurate records.

What we are looking for

We are looking for someone who:
- Has a genuine motivation and desire to improve the lives of children and young people.
- Has good communication and teamworking skills.
- Is aged 21 or over.

It would be great if you also have
- A Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare or equivalent, or are currently working towards one.
- Previous experience working in a children's residential setting.
- An understanding of trauma-informed or therapeutic approaches to care.
- A full UK driving licence.

Why join us?

Working in residential childcare is about much more than providing care. It's about being a consistent, trusted adult in a child's life and helping them develop the skills, confidence and relationships they need to move forward.

If you are compassionate, resilient and passionate about making a difference to children and young people, we would love to hear from you.

title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Role Overview

Affinity Staff is recruiting compassionate and reliable Healthcare Assistants (HCAs) to join our agency team, supporting an established care facility in Braintree, Essex.

As a temporary HCA working through Affinity Staff, you will play a vital role in providing high-quality personal care, dignity, and companionship to residents. You will enjoy complete control over your schedule while benefiting from our dedicated, round-the-clock support.

- Enhanced DBS check registered on the Update Service (or willing to process a new one).

- Caring, reliable nature with excellent communication skills.

Benefits of Working with Affinity Staff

- 24/7 Support: Dedicated consultants available round-the-clock to assist you.

How to Apply

Click Apply Now on CV-Library to join Affinity Staff or contact the Affinity Staff recruitment team to get registered immediately.

title: Night Care Assistant
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Care Assistant at a Barchester care home, you'll help residents enjoy each day by making sure they get the quality care and support they deserve. You'll assist with daily living, providing support and companionship and sharing great moments and memories too. It's a chance to bring your dedication and compassion to a fulfilling environment. Every day will be different, so you can expect to undertake work that's as varied as it is rewarding. As a Care Assistant, you could be doing anything from supporting residents with their food and drink and following care plans to ensuring that each of our residents has one-to-one time. To join us as a Care Assistant you'll need to have some experience of caring for older people, a can-do approach and excellent communication skills. Your empathy and warm-hearted approach will shine through, but above all, you'll have the compassion needed to deliver the highest standard of care and support for all our residents. In return we'll provide all the training you need to thrive.

REWARDS PACKAGE
In return for your dedication, you'll receive a competitive rate of pay plus our sector-leading benefits and rewards package including:
Free training and development for all roles
Access to wellbeing and support tools
A range of retail discounts and savings
Unlimited referrals with our Refer a Friend' bonus scheme
Employee of the Month' rewards and Long Service Awards'

And so much more!

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality care you'd expect for your loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

title: Residential Support Worker
description:
Are you a residential support worker with experience in supporting children If yes, this is a great opportunity for you.

An opportunity has arisen for Residential Support Worker to join a residential care provider supporting children and young people with learning disabilities and complex needs.

As a Residential Support Worker, you will provide nurturing, child-centered support, helping young people feel safe, develop independence and achieve positive outcomes.

This full-time permanent role offers a salary of up to £14 per hour and benefits. We are looking for multiple candidates.

What we are looking for
- Approx 1 year of experience supporting children and young people.
- Level 3 NVQ, Diploma qualification, or equivalent
- The ability to use trauma-informed and therapeutic approaches while maintaining appropriate boundaries.
- Committed to helping children and young people achieve positive outcomes.
- A full and verifiable employment history, with satisfactory references available.
- A current Enhanced DBS certificate.
- Right to work in the UK.

The candidates from the following background will be considered:
- Children's Residential Support Worker, Residential Support Worker, Support Worker, Care Worker, Children's Support Worker, Therapeutic Practitioner, Care Practitioner, Childcare Worker, Key Worker, Residential Care Worker or in a similar role.

This is a great opportunity for a Residential Support Worker to support young people, promote their development and make a positive difference in their lives.
